messages:
alex_support: FYI customer from APAC (acme.co.jp) reporting huge token auth latency and intermittent 401s. They provided traces showing requests landing in eu-west and timings ~2.4s for initial connect. Repro steps included curl from their office ISP.
jenna_support: Ticket #47832 linked — customer says headers include correct region header. They see `x-redwood-pop: eu-west-1` in responses. Asking if this could be DNS/geo issue. Customer willing to run commands.
sara_netops: Can you get the resolver IP they use and paste output of `dig +short @<resolver> api.redwood.ai` and `dig +trace api.redwood.ai`? Also `curl -I https://api.redwood.ai/health --resolve api.redwood.ai:<port>:<edge-ip>` would help. My first guess: EDNS/ISP caching or GeoIP DB mismatch at our DNS layer.
alex_support: Resolver IP: 203.54.12.77 (customer's office), they ran `dig` and got A 18.197.12.44 (eu-pop). They did `curl -v` and TLS handshake showed CN=eu-edge-1, so definitely hitting eu.
michael_sre: Two quick possibilities: 1) upstream resolver is returning a cached A record based on stale GeoIP mapping (resolver still-using older geoip), or 2) EDNS-Client-Subnet stripped by ISP -> our resolver sees a US/EU source. Also watch for NATs/proxies where public IP geolocation is wrong. Check our GeoIP DB version for that IP range and the recent ingest job.
tim_engineer: I ran an internal probe from apac-probe1: `curl -H "x-probe:apac-1" https://api.redwood.ai/ -sS -D -` and got `x-redwood-pop: eu-west-1`. Probe shows the request path included geo-fallback to eu-west because our routing policy flagged no apac capacity for model:small. There was a capacity spike last night and the fallback policy routed to cheapest compatible region (eu).
sara_netops: Thanks. That makes sense — if fallback kicks in we still want to route to nearest fallback, but clearly the geo decision logic used the probe/resolver mapping incorrectly. I pulled the GeoIP feed and the relevant ASN range was misclassified until ingest job at 2024-12-02 03:14 UTC. Our DB in prod may not have the update; check the DB version on the authoritative DNS nodes.
jenna_support: Customer ran `sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` and retested. They now report much better p99 latency (~120ms) and no 401s for two minutes, then it reverted back to eu-west after ~10m. They said their ISP uses Tier-1 caching with long TTLs.
michael_sre: That behavior screams resolver-side caching. Even if our authoritative switches answer, ISP cache holds the old record for the TTL. We should: 1) identify the TTL we published for that record during the outage window, 2) add an expedited invalidate via our CDN/DNS partner if possible, 3) add a targeted fallback rule for traffic coming from that resolver IP (203.54.12.0/24) to prefer apac for the next 30m while caches flush.
alex_support: Can we do targeted override for single customer/resolver? Customer is on a static IP block. They need immediate relief while we patch DB.
tim_engineer: Yes we can create a route tag keyed by upstream-resolver-ip in smart-routing and pin to apac-pop for that CIDR for 1h. I'll open change with approval. Patch will be low-risk but will require a hotfix to routing table and a short rollout.
ops-bot: INCIDENT_CREATED: INC-2024-3415 assigned to eng-net, severity P2, linked to ticket #47832.
deploy-bot: ROUTE_CHANGE: change-id rc-88211 created by tim_engineer, rollout started. Will push to 20% then 100% in 3 minutes if no errors.
jenna_support: Customer confirms after ~90s the `x-redwood-pop` header shows `apac-sg-1` and latency normalized. They still saw one 401 earlier but token validation logs show it was due to an unrelated clock skew at their edge (fixed). Customer is happy for now but wants follow-up.
michael_sre: Post-action items: 1) verify GeoIP DB ingestion and re-run on prod DNS nodes, 2) add monitor that correlates client IP geolocation -> pop mapping and fires if >1.5s additional latency and mismatch persists for >5m, 3) consider lowering TTL for geo records during high-churn windows or when model capacity rollouts are happening.
sara_netops: I'll deploy GeoIP DB bump to prod DNS nodes and validate against traceroutes for a sample of affected CIDRs. Also will request DNS partner to attempt cache purge for the resolver ASN.
alex_support: I'll follow up with customer summary and ask for permission to run additional probes from their office in next 24h. Thanks team — closing for now, will reopen if RC recurs. :thumbsup:
